text.p: Malta domestic demand slowed down in the first quarter of 1997 but earnings from tourism increased, Malta Central Bank said.
The bank, in its Quarterly Review publication, said the slackening of domestic demand could be due to a 0.3 percent unemployment rise and a 0.25 percent increase in retail price inflation.
Unemployment and inflation increases were due mainly to new indirect taxes introduced in January, the bank said.
Earnings from tourism were at 43.5 million Maltese pounds ($109 million), a 10 percent increase on the same period last year, it said.
Manufacturing sales for the first two months in 1997 dropped 11.2 percent to 114.5 million pounds, the bank added.
The balance of payements deficit shrank to 22.2 million pounds in the first quarter from 47.5 million in the same period in 1996 due to a drop in imports, the bank review showed.
